title: cuscuta planiflora var. callosa
intro: Cuscuta planiflora var. callosa, commonly known as Dodder, is a parasitic flowering plant that grows by attaching itself to the stems of other plants and obtaining its nutrients through haustoria. It has been traditionally used in medicine for its various health benefits, including its anti-inflammatory, antioxidant, and antidiabetic properties. The therapeutic actions of Dodder include its ability to regulate blood sugar levels, reduce oxidative stress, and exhibit antimicrobial activity, making it a potential treatment for various diseases. The bioactive constituents of Dodder include alkaloids, phenolic acids, and flavonoids, which are responsible for its medicinal properties.
